extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students in algebraic topology; readers learning H-spaces, Hopf algebras, and cohomology of Lie groups
extracted.subtask_short: study Hopf algebras and SO(n) cohomology
extracted.subtask_description: Understand the algebraic relationship between homology and cohomology for H-spaces (Pontryagin product and coproduct duality), the axioms and dualization of Hopf algebras, and compute/cocharacterize the (co)homology and Pontryagin/cup product structures of SO(n) and related Stiefel manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pontryagin product / coproduct duality criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an H–space and with coefficients in a field R the vector spaces H_n(X;R) are finite-dimensional for all n (or with R=Z and H_n(X;Z) finitely generated free for all n), then H^n(X;R)=Hom_R(H_n(X;R),R) and the Pontryagin product in homology and the coproduct in cohomology are dual to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: the coproduct in cohomology determines the Pontryagin product in homology and vice versa. Concretely, the coproduct Δ: H^*(X;R)→H^*(X;R)⊗H^*(X;R) is dual to the product H_*(X;R)⊗H_*(X;R)→H_*(X;R). This duality is used to deduce ring structures algebraically (e.g., deducing H^*(J(S^n);Z) is a polynomial ring from coproduct formulas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / axioms of a graded Hopf algebra (π, Δ, 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Hopf algebra structure on a graded R-module A is given by a product π:A⊗A→A, a coproduct Δ:A→A⊗A, and an element 1∈A^0 satisfying three conditions (1) 1 is two-sided identity for multiplication, (2) the coproduct has counit/projection properties (Δ(a)=a⊗1+1⊗a+∑a'_i⊗a''_i with specified projection properties), and (3) compatibility: Δ is an algebra homomorphism with the appropriate graded sign twist τ(a⊗b⊗c⊗d)=(−1)^{|b||c|}a⊗c⊗b⊗d so the diagram expressing Δ∘π = (π⊗π)∘τ∘(Δ⊗Δ) commutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three formal conditions capture identity, counit/projection, and multiplicative compatibility (graded bialgebra condition). The sign twist τ encodes the Koszul sign rule in graded contexts. Verifying these is the core of establishing a Hopf algebra structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite free graded-module hypothesis for dual Hopf algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a Hopf algebra over R that is a finitely generated free R-module in each degree, then the dual A^* inherits a Hopf algebra structure: the product and coproduct on A^* are the duals of Δ and π on A, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement of finite generation and freeness in each degree ensures Hom_R(−,R) identifies graded duals degreewise and that dual maps exist and satisfy Hopf axioms (conditions (1)-(3) dualize). This hypothesis is essential; without finite freeness dualization can fail or be ill-behaved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive elements determine coproduct/product when algebra generated by primitives
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Hopf algebra is generated (as an algebra) by primitive elements, then the product determines the coproduct (and hence the dual algebra) because primitives' coproducts are fixed (Δ(p)=p⊗1+1⊗p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This holds in many important examples (e.g., RP^∞, CP^∞, J(S^n) examples), allowing one to deduce dual algebra types (polynomial ↔ divided polynomial, exterior ↔ truncated polynomial) purely algebraically. Caveat: this is not true in general — there exist Hopf algebras whose algebra structure alone does not determine the coproduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity criterion for dual of polynomial algebra R[x]
rubrics_metrics.description: The dual Hopf algebra type of R[x] depends on the degree (parity) of x: if x is even-dimensional (or 2=0 in R), the dual is a divided polynomial algebra R[α] with α_i dual to x^i and multiplication rule α_i α_{n−i}=α_n; if x is odd-dimensional the dual decomposes differently (involving generators dual to x and its square y=x^2), producing a tensor product of divided polynomial parts corresponding to even-degree classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply (x⊗1+1⊗x)^n expansion and signs from graded-commutativity to read off coproduct structure; use this to compute cup products on spaces whose homology is R[x].

rubrics_metrics.name: H–space definition (homotopy identity condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A based CW complex X with basepoint e is an H–space if there exists a multiplication map μ:X×X→X such that the maps x↦μ(x,e) and x↦μ(e,x) are homotopic to the identity on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes this homotopy condition is taken as the definition rather than requiring strict identity. With these hypotheses, μ can be homotoped so that e becomes a strict two-sided identity. Use this when checking whether a given space admits H–space structure (e.g., spheres under certain dimension constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three criteria to produce a CW structure from characteristic maps ρφ_I
rubrics_metrics.description: Given maps ρφ_I: D^I→SO(n) indexed by admissible decreasing sequences I, they are characteristic maps of a CW structure if: (1) each ρφ_I is a homeomorphism from interior(D^I) onto its image; (2) the image cells are disjoint and cover the space; (3) the image of the boundary ρφ_I(∂D^I) lies in a union of cells of strictly lower dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three standard CW-construction checks (local homeomorphism on interiors, partition into cells, boundary attaches to lower skeleta) are the explicit checklist used to build the CW structure on SO(n) via the maps ρ coming from reflections. 'Admissible sequences' are decreasing sequences n>i1>...>im>0 (or single 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evaluation map p:SO(n)→S^{n−1} to analyze cell decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define p(α)=α(e_n). Then p restricts to a homeomorphism P^{n−1}−P^{n−2} → S^{n−1}−{e_n}, and the map h:(P^{n−1}−P^{n−2})×SO(n−1)→SO(n)−SO(n−1), h(v,α)=ρ(v)α, is a homeomorphism. This decomposition is used inductively in establishing the cell structure of SO(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the inductive step: SO(n) is built from SO(n−1) by attaching cells coming from P^{n−1}−P^{n−2} times SO(n−1). When proving cellularity or computing homology, use this local product/homeomorphism structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion relations among factor subspaces for cellular multiplication (P_iP_i ⊂ P_iP_{i−1} and P_iP_j ⊂ P_jP_i)
rubrics_metrics.description: To show the group multiplication is cellular and that ρ:P^{n−1}×...×P^1→SO(n) is cellular one needs the inclusions P_i P_i ⊂ P_i P_{i−1} and, for i<j, P_i P_j ⊂ P_j P_i (as subspaces of SO(n)). These are proven by expressing products of reflections r(v)r(w) as r(x)r(y) with appropriate dimensional control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These containment relations are the technical combinatorial/composition conditions that ensure products of cells land in appropriate skeleta so multiplication is cellular. They are used repeatedly to control where µ(e_I×e_J) lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality of cellular boundary maps with Z_2 coefficients implies cell basis for H^*(SO(n);Z_2)
rubrics_metrics.description: With Z_2 coefficients the cellular boundary maps for SO(n) are all trivial (inherited from P^i factors), hence H^*(SO(n);Z_2) has a Z_2 summand for each cell and the admissible monomials in the dual cell classes β_i form a basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: injectivity/surjectivity of the cellular map ρ on homology/cohomology, identification with truncated polynomial algebras on α_i under ρ^*, and combinatorial inductive arguments proving linear independence of admissible monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure theorem for H^*(SO(n);Z_2) (Theorem 3D.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) H^*(SO(n);Z_2) ≅ ⊗_{i odd} Z_2[β_i]/(β_i^{p_i}) where p_i is smallest power of 2 with |β_i^{p_i}| ≥ n; (b) The Pontryagin ring H_*(SO(n);Z_2) is the exterior algebra Z_2[e_1,...,e_{n−1}] with |e_i|=i and (e_i)^2=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: cohomology is tensor product of truncated polynomial algebras indexed by odd degrees; Pontryagin (homology) algebra is exterior. The proof uses cellular basis, relations β_{2i}=β_i^2 (when 2i<n), and vanishing when degree≥n. Use the inclusion relations and homeomorphisms f to prove commutativity/anticommutativity and primitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for primitivity of cohomology generators β_i
rubrics_metrics.description: Each cohomology generator β_i (dual to cellular homology class e_i) is primitive: Δ(β_i)=β_i⊗1+1⊗β_i. This follows because µ_*(e_I⊗e_J) lands in products P_IP_J and the only way to produce factor P_i after reordering is from e_i⊗e_0 or e_0⊗e_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primitivity is deduced from cellular multiplication and the inclusions controlling factor order; primitivity implies the Hopf algebra decompositions and explains the exterior/tensor-product structures in duals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular boundary pattern with integer coefficients (boundary formula for e_i)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the CW structure arising from P^{n−1}×...×P^1, the cellular boundary for e_i (in P^{i}) satisfies d e_i = 2 e_{i−1} for even i>0 and d e_i = 0 for odd i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit boundary pattern is used to split the cellular chain complex into small subcomplexes C_{2i}, to compute torsion (Z_2 summands) and free parts (Z summands) in H_*(SO(n);Z). It underlies the statement that H^*(SO(n);Z) is a direct sum of Z's and Z_2's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition/splitting criterion for integral chain complex of SO(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cellular chain complex C_*(SO(n)) splits as a tensor product of subcomplexes C_{2},C_{4},..., where each C_{2i} has basis {e_0,e_{2i},e_{2i-1},e_{2i}e_{2i-1}} (and C_{2k+1} when present). This yields H_*(SO(n);Z) as a direct sum of Z's (in certain dimensions) and Z_2's (in others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this splitting and the algebraic Künneth formula to deduce additive structure. This is the computational criterion to reduce the global chain complex into manageable factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pontryagin ring over Z (free part) is exterior on primitive generators
rubrics_metrics.description: The free (torsion-free) part H_*^{free}(SO(n);Z) is an exterior algebra Z[E_1,...,E_k] (and possibly an extra e_{2k+1}) where each generator E_i (e_{2i}e_{2i-1}) is primitive and satisfies graded-anticommutativity E_iE_j = −E_jE_i and (E_i)^2=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign computations are done by commuting factors using the homeomorphism f and tracking local degrees (signs). Once generators are shown primitive and to anticommute, the free Pontryagin algebra is exterior; dual Hopf algebra on cohomology free part is also exterior on the dual generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of CW structure on Stiefel manifolds via quotient projection
rubrics_metrics.description: For V_{n,k}=O(n)/O(n−k) (or SO(n)/SO(n−k)), the projection p:O(n)→V_{n,k} is cellular; cells in V_{n,k} are cosets e_I SO(n−k) (with n>i_1>...>i_m≥n−k) and the 0-cell is SO(n−k). The boundary of each cell lies in unions of lower-dimensional coset-cells, yielding a CW structure on V_{n,k}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cellularity of projection and the known CW structure on SO(n) to induce the CW structure on V_{n,k}. This allows transferring homology/cohomology calculations from SO(n) to V_{n,k} (e.g., computing H_*(V_{n,2}) explicitly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Bockstein homomorphisms to recover integer information from Z_p-cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: Bockstein homomorphisms provide extra structure on Z_p homology/cohomology that can sometimes recover torsion/exponent information lost when passing from Z to Z_p coefficients; they are introduced to connect Z_p computations to integer coefficient conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Z_p computations produce Z_p summands but integer homology might have Z_{p^n} torsion or other structure, analyze the Bockstein exact sequences and operations to lift information back to Z-coefficients. This is a standard technique when Z_p computations are easier.
